properties.corridor_name: Frederick Street to St Stephen's Church axis
properties.gradient: Steep north-falling glacial crag-and-tail slope descending ~35m toward the Water of Leith basin
properties.terminal_vista: St Stephen's Church (William Henry Playfair, 1827-1828) terminating the axis of St Vincent Street

properties.masonry_fabric: Craigleith and Hailes carboniferous sandstone ashlar, droved rustication on ground floors, coursed rubble to rear elevations
properties.roofing: Scotch blue-grey slate roofs with lead flashings, ashlar chimneys, cast-iron rainwater goods
properties.fenestration: Timber 12-pane (six-over-six) sash-and-case windows, cast-iron spearhead boundary railings and basement area lightwells

structures.name: Queen Street & North Frederick Street Georgian Tenement Terraces (Flanking)
St Stephen's Church (Terminal Focal Point)
structures.classification: Monumental Neoclassical parish church with square clock tower

properties.bedrock: Early Carboniferous sedimentary strata (Gullane Formation: sandstones, siltstones, and mudstones) cut by volcanic intrusive quartz-dolerite sills
properties.surficial_deposits: Stiff glacial till (boulder clay) overlying scoured bedrock, dry well-drained topsoils in Queen Street Gardens
properties.infrastructure: 18th-century subterranean vaulted cellarage, stone-lined barrel culverts, modern utilities embedded below whinstone setts
